With over a decade of teaching,Mrs.Bishop has many special memories of her students. But one story in particular stands ____.

"I taught Jerushi in 2013,”Mrs Bishop ____ "She was in Australia alone. Her parents had ____ behind in her home country.”Mrs Bishop supported Jerushi during Year 6 and encouraged her love of ____.A year later,she gave Mrs Bishop a beautiful landscape artwork she had painted.

Jerushi studied in Australia for ____ few years, but Mrs Bishop lost touch with her ____ she went back home. Then,a few years ago,Jerushi ____ out to Mrs Bishop. At the time, Jerushi's painting was ____ above Mrs Bishop's desk—proof that Mrs Bishop had ____ forgotten her.

"Jerushi told me she was now studying to ____ a teacher just like me,”Mrs Bishop says.“It was a beautiful message. As a teacher,you often don't realise the kind of ____ you can have.”

It was a full-cirele moment for Mrs Bishop,who remembers ____ her own teacher a letter five years ago with a ____ message,saying she started her teaching career because of him."His passion ____ teaching really inspired me."For Mrs Bishop,teaching is both a pleasure and a privilege.“When parents thank me,I ____ them,'No, thank you for allowing me to be a part of your child’s life.'”

Last week,a friend from Colorado, who I first met in Thailand, came into town for his sister's graduation. He called me and we met up in a bar. It was one of the best nights of the summer. We retold stories from our time in Thailand, drank a couple beers, and just reflected in the presence of one another. And the best part:he was doing well, succeeding in life while pursuing his dreams.

On my way home from seeing him on his last night in town, I got a little depressed. I just forgot how much fun I had with him and why he made my Thailand experience so awesome.And that of course go me missing all my friends: the ones sillin Santa Clara, the ones following their music careers, the ones living in Portland that I have just been too dumb to contact. I have just been so caught up in writing, studying for the GRE,lounging about my house, that I haven't made the effort that I certainly should have.

Sometimes, we get so absorbed in our own lives that we forget what makes our lives worth living. nans are social creatures. It is in our DNA.Evolutionary psychologists suggest that because we relied upon social groups in primitive times to survive,we have a negative biological reaction to loneliness today.

So go out there and contact a friend you haven't talked to for a while. If nothing else,just check in to see how they're doing. Because even if you haven't spoken for a while,I'm certain that they are thinking of you.

Seagulls(海鸥)don't just steal food from tourists;they also make quite a mess on the boats of the Australian National Maritime Museum. Seagull droppings stain the boats, causing the museum staff to spend many hours cleaning up the mess left by the seagulls.

After many failed attempts at keeping the annoying seagulls away, the staff had a brilliant idea. Inspired by the method used at various airports to drive away wildlife, they sought out the Australian Dog Working Centre and adopted Bailey. The three-year-old dog was appointed the new position of Assistant Director of Seagulls and put to work.

The highlight of Bailey's morning is chasing the seagulls away from the boats. For the first few weeks, Bailey was a little too enthusiastic about his new role and managed to jump into the water during the pursuit of seagulls. But it wasn't long before he was fitted with a new work uniform—a bright yellow life vest that keeps him floating on water. Bailey even has a special staff ID with his photo and the title of his important position. He has had to get familiar with the museum's waterfront, which he patrols(巡查)frequently. This is especially important at night when there is no human activity around to scare the seagulls off.

The museum staff members are all very fond of Bailey,making sure to give him lots of playtime, walks and affection. He is very well taken care of,with visits to the local animal doctor for grooming(梳毛)scheduled every two weeks.

When he is clocked on, Bailey prefers not to be disturbed so he can focus on his job.However, when he is not working, the museum encourages all visitors to come to say hello to their special employee. So the next time you visit the museum,make sure to say hello to this hardworking dog!

The recent wildfire in Alberta,Canada, has already burned through 600 square miles of land, and 20of houses in the city of Fort McMurray; all its 88,000 residents have left their homes. But how do you put out fires this big and intense?

Wind, fuel and the slope(坡度)of the land are three vital factors. You can't do very much about the first one. The firefighters will be paying attention to weather conditions. In an ideal world, the wind would force the flames back on to ground that has already been burmed.

Fuel—mainly the trees—can be managed in several ways,such as bulldozing(铲除)it out of the way or starting controlled fires to burn it off so it can't feed the main fire.

The slope of the land can also help. Fires burn much more aggressively going uphill than they do downhill.You don't try to fight a fire going uphill. The firefighters will be looking very carefully how they arrange their personnel and equipment on a downhill side of a slope.In a fire that is relatively small and moving downhill, you can launch a direct attack,physically beating the flames out with special tools. You would come in behind the fire,so you're not face to face with flames coming towards you.

In addition, fire can spread a large distance away from the fire-front by burning embers(余火) carried on the wind, which then start other fires elsewhere.You can actively work on preventing parts of the fire going in certain directions. But this requires resources,such as water bombers—planes that can dump vast quantities of water. They aren't just flying over the top of the fire and releasing water.They usually wet the fuel ahead of the fire or along its sides to stop the spread of the fire.

Pittsburgh Arlington,an elementary school in the state of Pennsylvania, is battling chronic absence from school with a community-centered approach that combines care, connection,and practical support. Over half of the school's 353 students frequently miss classes, Many of these students face barriers like a lack of transportation, which the school district does not provide for those living less than a mile and a half away.

To tackle this issue, the school worked with the Brashear Association,a local nonprofit, to launch the nanas(保姆)program. This initiative provides a personal touch, where nanas make cheerful morning wakeup calls to families,often ending the conversation with a heartfelt"I love you."In addition, the program offers ree bus rides to and from school,ensuring that children who might otherwise miss school can attend regularly.

The program currently serves 36 children daily, but demand is high, with about 20 students still on the waitlist. Principal Crystal Caldwell wishes there were more resources to expand the service. Meanwhile, the school is also working on other solutions, like paying staff to walk students home and working together with a nearby church to offer before-school care.

These efforts are part of a broader initiative aiming at making school a friendly and desirable place for students. This includes working with local arts organizations to create interesting programs and offering regular motivational talks to encourage attendance(出勤). These combined efforts reflect a deep understanding that the causes are complex and varied, requiring the entire community’s involvement to address them effectively.

Tiffini Gorman, director of partnerships at the nonprofit A+ Schools,emphasizes the importance of collective responsibility in ensuring that every child has the support they need to succeed. The school's approach highlights the significance of community involvement in creating a positive and supportive environment for students.

Counting butterflies can reduce anxiety and boost a sense of connection with nature,a study has found. Researchers surveyed participants in the Big Butterfly Count in 2022,in which wildlife charity Butterfly Conservation encouraged people to spend 15 minutes outside counting butterflies to help scientists track how the insects were faring. Surveys completed by 382 people before and after the three-week count period revealed a9 per cent reduction in anxiety among participants,and a greater sense of connection with nature,as well as noticing butterflies and nature more.

Further surveys completed by 345 people,which were sent five weeks after the count, did not find nature connectedness and reduced anxiety had been maintained. But they revealed an increase in general wellbeing compared with before the project. The research, published in the journal Biological Conservation,was carried out by Butterfly Conservation and the University of Derby.

The surveys revealed people had a range of positive and negative emotions associated with taking part,ranging from joy and fascination to sadness and concern about declining insects. Richard Fox, head of science at Butterfly Conservation, said, "This study is the first to prove that the simple act of looking for and counting butterlies leads to a decrease in anxiety. The results suggest that citizen science projects can play a part in improving people's mental health,as well as gathering important data on how butterflies are faring to inform our conservation work.”

Carly Butler, lead researcher on the study,said the benefits of reduced anxiety and stronger connectedness with nature were the same whether people just carried out one 15-minute count or did so multiple times. Dr Butler added that participants felt motivated to help butterflies and nature by doing things such as making their gardens butterfly-friendly.

questions.explanation: 本题考查辅音字母组合th的发音。tooth、wealth、truth中的th均发清辅音/θ/，而smooth中的th发浊辅音/ð/，与其他三项不同。故选B。
本题考查字母s的发音。answer、absence、escape中的s均发/s/，而disease中的s发/z/，与其他三项不同。故选D。

questions.stem: Let's celebrate the victory of our team in the sports meeting,____?
questions.explanation: 本题考查反义疑问句。句意：让我们庆祝我们队在运动会上取得的胜利，好吗？以Let's开头的祈使句，附加疑问部分用shall we；以Let us开头的祈使句，附加疑问部分用will you。故选D。

questions.stem: ____is late for the examination will not be allowed to enter the classroom.
questions.explanation: 本题考查主语从句。句意：无论谁考试迟到，都不允许进入教室。分析句子结构可知，空格处引导主语从句，且在从句中作主语。whoever意为“无论谁、不管什么人”，可引导主语从句并作主语，符合句意和用法。who意为“谁”，通常用于疑问或特指已知的某个人，不符合句意；whom可引导主语从句，但在句中作宾语，不符合用法；no matter who只能引导让步状语从句，不能引导主语从句。故选A。

questions.stem: ____the project on time, they had to work late into the night for several days.
questions.explanation: 本题考查非谓语动词。句意：为了按时完成项目，他们不得不熬夜工作了好几天。分析句子结构可知，本句已有谓语动词，故空格处应用非谓语动词。过去分词表示被动或完成，动词不定式表示目的或将来，现在分词表示主动、进行或伴随。空格处表示目的，应用动词不定式。故选C。

questions.stem: —Where do you usually have your hair____? —At the barber's near the grocery.
questions.explanation: 本题考查固定用法。句意：——你通常在哪里理发？——在杂货店旁边的理发店。have sth. done为固定用法，意为“让某事被做”，done与sth.之间为动宾关系。cut的原形、过去式、过去分词同形。故选A。

questions.stem: In the digital era, it is very important not to____personal information on the Internet.
questions.explanation: 本题考查短语辨析。句意：在数字时代，避免在网上泄露个人信息至关重要。try out意为“测试”；give out意为“泄露、公布、发布”；pick out意为“挑选、辨认出”；keep out意为“不进入、留在外面”。故选B。

questions.stem: With more colleagues to help you with the task,you will be relieved____pressure.
questions.explanation: 本题考查固定搭配。句意：有更多同事帮你完成这项任务，你的压力将会得到缓解。relieve...of...为固定搭配，意为“减轻……的……（负担、压力等）、解除……的……（困扰、责任等）”，此处为其被动结构。故选B。

questions.stem: I cannot afford a dinner in that fancy restaurant. Let's try a____expensive one.
questions.explanation: 本题考查形容词比较级。句意：我负担不起那家高档餐厅的晚餐。我们找一家便宜点的餐厅试试吧。此处表示两者进行比较，应用比较级，故排除A、C两项。根据句意可知，此处表示“更便宜的”，“less+原级”为否定意义的比较级，意为“不那么……”（相当于not as/so...as），less expensive意为“更便宜的”。故选D。

questions.stem: Writing poetry about country life____her from the boredom of everyday life.
questions.explanation: 本题考查动词辨析。句意：写关于乡村生活的诗歌使她摆脱了日常生活的无聊。remind意为“提醒、使想起”；benefit意为“使受益”；liberate意为“解放、使解脱”，liberate sb. from sth.为固定用法，意为“把某人从某事中解放出来”；persuade意为“劝说、说服”。故选C。

questions.stem: ____there was no obvious evidence against him,most people thought he was guilty.
questions.explanation: 本题考查状语从句。句意：尽管没有明显证据指控他，但大多数人认为他有罪。根据句意可知，空格处引导让步状语从句，表示“虽然、尽管”。unless意为“除非”；if意为“如果”；while意为“虽然、尽管”；because意为“因为”。故选C。

questions.stem: He____at the company for five years before he was promoted to a management position.
questions.explanation: 本题考查时态。句意：他在被提拔到管理岗位之前，已经在这家公司工作了五年。主句动作“工作”发生在从句动作“被提拔”之前，从句动作已是过去时，故主句动作应用过去完成时。故选A。

questions.stem: The decision finally came from the manager____all staff should work extra hours.
questions.explanation: 本题考查同位语从句。句意：最终经理作出了所有员工都应加班这一决定。分析句子结构可知，空格处引导的是同位语从句，解释decision的具体内容。同位语从句中不缺少成分，且意义完整，应用that引导。故选D。

questions.stem: Paul's poor performance in the interview was a big____to his mother, who had wanted her son to study at Harvard University.
questions.explanation: 本题考查名词辨析。句意：保罗面试表现糟糕，这对一心想让儿子上哈佛大学的母亲来说是一个重大打击。act意为“行为、行动”；blow意为“打击、挫折”，a big blow to sb.是固定用法，意为“对某人的沉重打击”；sign意为“迹象、征兆”；air通常作不可数名词，意为“空气”。故选B。

questions.stem: She is the only one in the office____can speak English fluently.
questions.explanation: 本题考查定语从句。句意：她是办公室里唯一能流利说英语的人。分析句子结构可知，空格处为定语从句的引导词，且在从句中作主语。先行词为the only one且指人，从句引导词应用that/who。故选D。

questions.stem: With the help of the____glasses,people now can have a virtual tour of the museums around the world while sitting at home.
questions.explanation: 本题考查形容词辨析。句意：借助智能眼镜，人们现在可以坐在家里虚拟游览世界各地的博物馆。smart意为“智能的”；neat意为“整洁的”；mobile意为“可移动的”；old意为“老的、年纪大的”。故选A。

questions.stem: The doctor strongly recommends that the patient____a strict diet to keep healthy.
questions.explanation: 本题考查虚拟语气。句意：医生强烈建议病人遵循严格的饮食以保持健康。表示建议、要求、命令等的动词后的宾语从句常用虚拟语气，从句谓语动词用“should+动词原形”，should可以省略。故选C。
短语辨析题。本句句意：比西普夫人有十余年的教学经历，有许多关于学生们的特别回忆，但有一个故事尤为突出。stand up意为“站起来”；stand out意为“显眼、突出”；stand on意为“依赖、坚持”；stand by意为“袖手旁观、支持”。故选B。
动词辨析题。本句句意：“我在2013年教过杰鲁西，”比西普夫人回忆道。argue意为“争论、争吵”；recall意为“记起、回忆起”；suggest意为“建议、提议”；repeat意为“重复、重说”。故选B。
固定搭配题。本句句意：她的父母留在了她的祖国。go意为“去、走”；hide意为“藏、隐蔽”；stay意为“停留、待”；look意为“看、瞧”。联系上文可知，此处表示“她的父母留在国内，没有和她一同前往澳大利亚”，stay behind为固定搭配，意为“留下来，不离开”，符合句意。故选C。
理解推断题。本句句意：六年级期间，比西普夫人一直支持着杰鲁西，并激发了她对艺术的热爱。sport意为“体育运动”；maths意为“数学”；music意为“音乐”；art意为“艺术”。根据下文的landscape artwork(风景画)可知，比西普夫人激发了杰鲁西对艺术的热爱。故选D。
限定词和副词辨析题。本句句意：杰鲁西在澳大利亚又学习了几年，但她一回国，比西普夫人就与她失去了联系。another为限定词，意为“又一、再一”；too为副词，意为“太、过于”；every为限定词，意为“每个”；so为副词，意为“那样、如此”。another few years意为“又几年”，符合句意。故选A。
连词辨析题。本句句意：杰鲁西在澳大利亚又学习了几年，但她一旦回国，比西普夫人就与她失去了联系。although意为“虽然、尽管”；unless意为“除非”；once意为“一……就”；until意为“直到……为止”。故选C。
固定搭配题。本句句意：然后，几年前，杰鲁西联系了比西普夫人。reach意为“到达、联系”；check意为“检查”；call意为“大声呼叫”；move意为“移动”。reach out to sb.和call out to sb.均为固定搭配，前者意为“与某人联系”，后者意为“向某人大喊”。故选A。
动词辨析题。本句句意：那时，杰鲁西的画还挂在比西普夫人的桌子上方，这证明了比西普夫人从未忘记她。install意为“安装”；hang意为“悬挂、吊”；locate意为“确定……的准确地点”；rank意为“把……分等级”。故选B。
副词辨析题。本句句意：那时，杰鲁西的画还挂在比西普夫人的桌子上方，这证明了比西普夫人从未忘记她。since意为“此后、后来”；ever意为“曾经”；just意为“正好、刚才”；never意为“从未、未曾”。故选D。
动词辨析题。本句句意：杰鲁西告诉我她现在正在学习如何成为一名像我一样的老师。become意为“成为”；train意为“训练、培训”；find意为“发现、碰到”；respect意为“尊敬、尊重”。故选A。
名词辨析题。本句句意：作为一名老师，你常常意识不到自己能产生怎样的影响。duty意为“责任、义务”；impact意为“巨大影响、强大作用”；right意为“权利、公正”；hope意为“希望、期望”。故选B。
动词辨析题。本句句意：对比西普夫人来说，这是一个圆满的时刻——她记得五年前曾给自己的老师写过一封信，传达了类似的信息，说是因为这位老师她才开始了自己的教学生涯。lend意为“借给、借出”；promise意为“许诺、保证”；write意为“书写”；order意为“命令、订购”。故选C。
形容词辨析题。本句句意：对比西普夫人来说，这是一个圆满的时刻——她记得五年前曾给自己的老师写过一封信，传达了类似的信息，说是因为这位老师她才开始了自己的教学生涯。similar意为“类似的”；previous意为“先前的”；secret意为“秘密的”；vague意为“模糊的”。故选A。
固定搭配题。本句句意：他对教学的热情真正激励了我。passion for sth.为固定搭配，意为“对……的热爱或热情”。故选C。
动词辨析题。本句句意：当家长们感谢我时，我告诉他们：“不，谢谢你们允许我成为你们孩子生命的一部分。”ask意为“问、询问”；warn意为“警告、提醒”；advise意为“劝告、建议”；tell意为“告诉、告知”。故选D。

questions.stem: What did the author and his friend do in the bar?
options: They recalled their time in Thailand.
They talked about the joy of graduation.
They exchanged views on career success.
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。根据文章第一段第二句和第二段第一句可知，作者和朋友在一家酒吧见了面，并回忆了他们在泰国的那段时光。故选A。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the author from Paragraph 3?
options: He has achieved success in writing.
He has got a high score on the GRE.
He does not enjoy his life in Portland.
He regrets not having seen his friends.
questions.explanation: 推理判断题。根据文章第三段第一句可知，作者有点儿沮丧，接下来作者给出了沮丧的原因，即作者在与朋友见面后，因回忆起往日的快乐而感到失落，并对自己因忙碌而疏于联系朋友感到后悔与自责。由此可推断，作者后悔没有见他的朋友们。故选D。

questions.stem: What is a cause of humans'negative biological reaction to loneliness?
questions.explanation: 推理判断题。根据文章第四段最后一句可知，进化心理学家认为，由于我们在原始时代依赖社会群体生存，因此如今孤独会引起消极的生理反应。由此可推断，人们对社会支持的依赖导致人类对孤独产生了消极的生理反应。故选B。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest in the passage?
options: Relying on friends for social success.
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章最后一段提到，去联系一位许久未交谈的朋友吧，如果没什么特别的事，就去问候一下他们的近况吧。由此可知，作者建议读者与朋友们保持联系。故选B。

questions.stem: What troubles the Australian National Maritime Museum?
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章第一段最后一句提到，海鸥的排泄物弄脏了船，导致博物馆工作人员花费大量时间清理海鸥留下的排泄物。由此可知，鸟类的排泄物让澳大利亚国家海事博物馆很困扰。故选C。

questions.stem: What is Bailey's job at the museum?
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章第二段最后一句提到贝利被任命为“海鸥事务助理总监”，第三段第一句提到贝利早上的工作重点是把海鸥从船上赶走。由此可知，贝利在博物馆的工作是驱赶海鸥。故选D。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Bailey?
options: He is often disturbed by tourists.
He enjoys working instead of playing.
He becomes the symbol of the museum.
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章第四段第二句提到，贝利得到了很好的照顾，每两周就会由当地的动物医生为其梳毛。由此可知，贝利定期接受身体护理。故选A。

questions.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the underlined expression“clocked on”in the last paragraph?
questions.explanation: 词义理解题。文章最后一段第一句提到，当贝利“打卡上班”时，他不喜欢被打扰，以便专心工作。由此可推断，clock on意为“打卡上班”，与下文的when he is not working(当他不工作的时候)相呼应。off duty意为“下班”；in bed意为“在床上”；under control意为“处于控制之下”；at work意为“在工作”。故选D。

questions.stem: Which factor is mainly talked about in Paragraph 2?
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章第二段提到，风、燃料和地面坡度是三个关键因素，人们对第一个因素几乎无能为力。消防员会密切关注天气状况。理想情况下，风会将火焰吹回已经烧过的区域。由此可知，本段主要讨论的是“wind(风)”。故选B。

questions.stem: Why should trees be bulldozed in firefighting?
options: To put out a controlled fire.
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。文章第三段提到，燃料(主要是树木)可通过推土机铲除或可控燃烧等方式处理，目的是使其不能助长火势。由此可知，在灭火时铲除树木是为了防止火势蔓延。故选C。

questions.stem: When can firefighters directly attack a fire?
options: When it is small and moving downhill.
When it is big and moving sideways.
When the trees ahead of it are wet.
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。根据文章第四段第五句可知，对于相对较小且向下坡蔓延的火势，可以采取直接灭火的方法，使用专门的工具将火焰扑灭。故选A。

questions.stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the underlined word“dump”in the last paragraph?
questions.explanation: 词义理解题。文章最后一段最后三句提到，灭火飞机可以倾倒大量水。它们不仅仅是飞越火场上空洒水。通常它们会提前浇湿火势前方的燃料或火场两侧区域，以阻止火势蔓延。由此可推断，dump意为“倾倒”。drop意为“使落下”；boil意为“煮沸”；absorb意为“吸收”；produce意为“生产、制造”。故选A。

questions.stem: What problem is Pittsburgh Arlington trying to solve?
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。根据文章第一段第一句可知，匹兹堡阿灵顿小学正在通过一种以社区为中心的方法来应对学生长期缺勤的问题。故选C。

questions.stem: What measure does the nanas program take to help students come to school?
questions.explanation: 事实细节题。根据文章第二段最后一句可知，“保姆计划”还提供往返学校的免费巴士接送服务，确保那些原本可能缺勤的学生能够正常出勤。故选C。

questions.stem: What does the underlined word“This” in Paragraph 4 refer to?
questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。词义理解题。第四段第一句指出“这些努力是一项更宏大倡议(a broader initiative)的一部分”，紧接着“This includes working with local arts organizations...”中的This即指代前文的这一更宏大的倡议。故选B。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）

options: Nanas help find a new approach to teaching art

questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。主旨大意题。全文讲述匹兹堡阿灵顿小学联合社区各方力量（保姆计划、免费巴士接送、与教堂和艺术组织合作等）共同应对学生长期缺勤问题，帮助孩子们回到课堂。D项“共同努力让孩子们回到课堂”最能概括全文主旨。故选D。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）

questions.stem: Why were people encouraged to participate in the Big Butterfly Count?
options: To help with a science project.
questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。事实细节题。根据第一段可知，该活动鼓励人们花15分钟在户外数蝴蝶，以帮助科学家了解蝴蝶等昆虫的生存状况，属于公民科学项目，即帮助一项科学项目。故选D。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）

questions.stem: What did further surveys find?
options: People felt more excited about wildlife.
People were closer to the natural world.
People were more generous and helpful.
questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。事实细节题。根据第二段可知，计数结束五周后的进一步调查显示，与大自然亲近感和焦虑减轻的效果未能保持，但与项目开始前相比，参与者的总体幸福感有所提升。故选A。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）

questions.stem: What were people concerned about according to the surveys?
options: Their inability to gather enough data.
Their anxiety in doing the surveys.
The duration of the counting task.
questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。事实细节题。根据第三段可知，参与者的情绪从快乐、着迷到悲伤、对昆虫数量减少（declining insects）的担忧不等，即人们担忧蝴蝶种群的减少。故选B。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）

questions.stem: What can people do to help butterflies and nature according to the last paragraph?
options: Turn butterfly counting into a routine.
Make their gardens fit for butterflies.
Persuade their friends to help butterflies.
questions.explanation: 【注】原文件答案解析在第49题后截断，本题为依据原文推断。事实细节题。根据最后一段可知，巴特勒博士提到参与者感到有动力去帮助蝴蝶和大自然，例如让自己的花园对蝴蝶友好（making their gardens butterfly-friendly），即使花园变得适合蝴蝶。故选C。（注：本题官方解析页在原PDF中缺失，此答案系依据原文推断，仅供参考）
